clue.text: Self-consciousness?

parts.note: read literally, an awareness of oneself in the physical sense: how one sees one's own figure and looks

explanation.surface: A question about feeling shy or awkward in company.
explanation.walkthrough: Self-consciousness usually means awkwardness; the question mark invites the literal reading, consciousness of the self as a physical form.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a person's perception of their own physical appearance, a literal awareness of how the self looks.

clue.text: Support Kelvin's leaving for northern town

indicators.note: Kelvin is leaving, so its letter departs from the word for support

parts.note: backup is support or reinforcement
K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit

explanation.surface: Someone backs a scientist moving away to the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes K out of BACKUP. BACUP is a mill town in Lancashire, in the north of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacup is a small Lancashire town in the north of England, in the Rossendale valley.

clue.text: Fatal lapse?

parts.note: a moral failing that, in Christian teaching, kills the soul: one of the seven gravest wrongs

explanation.surface: A slip with deadly consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an accident; theologically, the seven gravest sins are called mortal or deadly because they bring spiritual death.
explanation.definitionFit: Pride, envy, gluttony and the rest are the seven moral failings traditionally said to bring spiritual death.

clue.text: Made it more difficult to appear extreme

indicators.note: difficult here suggests the letters are troubled or awkward, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complicated matters so much that they seemed over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges the ten letters of MADE IT MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immoderate goes beyond reasonable limits, just as an extreme view does.

clue.text: Inform primate about pair on island

indicators.note: the primate goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

explanation.surface: Telling a monkey about a couple living on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the primate round the pair and island; 'on' places pair above island, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To apprise someone is to tell them or make them aware, a formal synonym of inform.

clue.text: Notable issue in which three quarters must be invested

indicators.note: investing something puts it inside, as one invests money in a fund, so these letters go in

parts.note: to issue is to emit or send out
N, E and N are compass quarters (points): north, east, north

explanation.surface: A significant matter in which seventy-five per cent has to be put in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests fractions, but quarters are compass points, and 'must be invested' puts three of them inside the word for issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eminent is distinguished and well known, as a notable figure is.

clue.text: Flap associated with American banker in Europe

parts.note: a tag is a loose flap or tab

explanation.surface: A flap attached to a US financier working in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, which has banks; the Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is a long Iberian river, and a river is a banker since it has banks.

clue.text: Nick's bearing off duck

indicators.note: the bearing goes off, that is it is removed from the word

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
S, south, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A man called Nick's posture puts off a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes S from STEAL. Nick looks like a name but is the verb meaning to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling duck.

clue.text: Get hold of English beef

parts.note: to grip is to get hold of

explanation.surface: An instruction to grab some British meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' is not meat: as a verb or noun it is slang for a complaint, as is gripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a complaint or grumble.

clue.text: Conscious about male viewpoint

indicators.note: the word for conscious goes about, around, the letter for male

parts.note: sentient means able to feel, conscious

explanation.surface: Someone aware of what a man thinks.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTIENT wraps round M.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is an opinion or attitude, a point of view.

clue.text: Person who's silent about one's allegation

indicators.note: the silent person goes about, around, the letter for one

parts.note: a clam is someone who says nothing, as in 'clam up'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A quiet person keeps their accusation to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAM wraps round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is an assertion of something as fact, often unproven, as an allegation is.

clue.text: President, one against reinforcing quota to answer need

indicators.note: reinforcing a thing means going into it to strengthen it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share or quota
I is the Roman numeral one
V, versus, means against

explanation.surface: A president and someone opposed boosting allowances to meet demand.
explanation.walkthrough: IV goes inside RATION after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Privation is a lack of the necessities of life, a state of want or need.

clue.text: Support layer-erroneously deliver one with inclusive reduced price

indicators.note: the letters are put together wrongly, in a mistaken order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
price cut short to its abbreviation PR

explanation.surface: A request to deliver one item at a cut-price rate, all-inclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneously' rearranges DELIVER with I and PR, the abbreviation of price, 'with inclusive' joining them in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile driver is a machine that hammers piles, the posts that lay foundations, into the ground.

clue.text: Resentment's overcome after positive spirit is shown

indicators.note: the resentment comes after the letter for positive
overcome as in turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger or resentment

explanation.surface: Bitterness is conquered once an upbeat attitude is displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcome' turns IRE to ERI. A peri is a fairy or spirit of Persian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian mythology a peri is a beautiful supernatural being, a kind of fairy or sprite.

clue.text: Official agency caught informer

parts.note: a bureau is an office or agency
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: Government department nabs a snitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureaucrat is an administrator in a government office, an official.

clue.text: Bank book

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is a store kept back, a bank; to book a seat or table is to reserve it.

clue.text: Rest of servicemen on guard outside African capital

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army servicemen

indicators.note: the guard goes outside, around, the capital letter

parts.note: a minder is a bodyguard

indicators.note: a capital is the first letter, here of African

explanation.surface: Soldiers stand guard beyond an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African capital' looks like a city, but it is the capital (first) letter A, which MINDER goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Right about very loud pupil being sweet

indicators.note: the word for right goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: true means correct, right
FF, fortissimo, means very loud in music
L, learner, stands for a pupil, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A noisy schoolchild turns out to be a sweetie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the word for right round the very loud and pupil letters; L for pupil comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is a rich chocolate confection, a sweet.

clue.text: Offer put in for private room-not allowed

indicators.note: the offer is put in between the other pieces

parts.note: a den is a private room for retreat
a bid is an offer

explanation.surface: A tender submitted for a private room is refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden is prohibited, banned.

clue.text: Track idiot seized by old Arab

indicators.note: the idiot is seized, held inside, by the old Arab

parts.note: a Moor was a medieval North African Muslim, the historical sense of Arab here
nit is a British word for an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool is captured by an ancient warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old Arab' calls on the medieval Moors of North Africa and Spain; 'seized by' puts the idiot inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to keep track of it, observe it over time.

clue.text: Crash course for shoplifters?

parts.note: a crash course is usually intensive teaching; here, a raid where thieves crash a vehicle into a shop

explanation.surface: Quick lessons for shop thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crash course' usually means quick tuition; read literally it is a course of action involving crashing a car through a shopfront to steal goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram raid is a robbery in which a vehicle is driven into a shop window to gain entry.

clue.text: Clown's one blunder, landing in a hole

indicators.note: the pieces end up landing inside the hole

parts.note: a pot is a hole, as a pocket on a billiard table
I is the Roman numeral one
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A clown's mistake is falling into a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landing in' puts one and blunder inside the hole; the 's of 'Clown's' means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Fuss over key culinary ingredient

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another sits above it

parts.note: pother is an old word for a fuss or commotion
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A chef makes a fuss over the essential element of a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like an adjective meaning essential; it is the musical key B.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a leafy plant cooked or used to flavour food, an item in the kitchen.

clue.text: One new order for small length

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A single new arrangement for a short stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the Order of the Companions of Honour, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, a twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Not forthcoming about the French swimmer

indicators.note: the word for reticent goes about, around, the French article

parts.note: coy means reticent, not forthcoming
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Being reserved about the French fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Coley is a fish common in British waters, sold cheaply as an alternative to cod.
explanation.definitionFit: Coley is a fish of the cod family, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: I use Martha, trained, but not professional

indicators.note: trained means shaped or worked on, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone employs Martha, who is qualified yet still lacks polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges the letters of I USE MARTHA; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is done unskilfully, lacking the polish of a paid expert.

clue.text: Joint in Bayreuth-in Germany

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A connection found in a Bavarian city of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'BayreutH IN GErmany'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinge is a movable joint, such as the one a door swings on.

clue.text: No longer a member of church

parts.note: being on a team or board means being a member of it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has left their church congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on', as in on the committee, signals membership; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time past, as no longer suggests used of what was.

clue.text: Determine energy policy in time

indicators.note: the energy and policy go in the time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
E is the physics symbol for energy
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Set out an energy strategy within a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to define or mark out precisely, to fix the limits of.

clue.text: Sculptor seen in Cairo diner

indicators.note: the name is seen in, lying within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A famous artist spotted in an Egyptian restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'CaiRO DINer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Auguste Rodin was a French sculptor, maker of The Thinker.

clue.text: Heard Frost's poetry

indicators.note: heard signals that the word must be listened to rather than read

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: Someone listened to verse by the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: Frost looks like the American poet; it is rime, ice crystals, which sounds the same as the word for verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is verse, poetry with matching line endings.

clue.text: Society girl's opening bet

parts.note: a debut is a first appearance or opening
an ante is a stake or bet in poker

explanation.surface: A young socialite places her first wager.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman formally introduced into society.
